metadata.dominant_domain_inferred: long-form personal-finance, money-psychology and real-estate essays for a German audience
metadata.core_promise_of_system: Make abstract money topics feel urgent, personal, morally loaded and immediately actionable by translating the German macroeconomy into high-stakes life consequences.
metadata.primary_content_engine: History/metaphor-driven warning essay that reframes a familiar financial idea as misunderstood, structurally rigged, psychologically dangerous, and still navigable if the viewer adopts the creator's framework.
metadata.character_length_rule: The final FULL SCRIPT must be no less than 7,000 characters and no more than 9,000 characters.

audience_inference.knowledge_level: intermediate aspirational retail investor / financially anxious knowledge worker, familiar with Girokonto, Tagesgeld, Festgeld, Bausparvertrag, ETF-Sparplan, gesetzliche Rentenversicherung, Riester, Rürup and mortgages but unsure of the whole picture
audience_inference.psychological_state: skeptical, economically uneasy, wants clarity and edge, feels mainstream advice (Sparkasse, Volksbank, finanzen.net, Finanztest, ARD/ZDF, simplified guidance) is incomplete or too late
audience_inference.aspirational_identity: calm, informed, anti-hype, system-level thinker who spots traps before the crowd — someone who understands the German game beyond 'save in a Bausparvertrag and buy a house'

channel_persona.role: translator of hidden financial mechanics inside the German system
channel_persona.voice: calm but severe, analytical but conversational, anti-guru while still authoritative
authority_basis: claims personal investing experience in Germany

references long study time and obscure documents (BaFin regulations, Bundesbank reports, ECB minutes, Statistisches Bundesamt data, Sachverständigenrat reports, Stiftung Warentest, Verbraucherzentrale, federal budgets)
uses German and global historical analogies
frames advice as mechanical, not motivational
signals distance from schemes, courses and hype
mentions hands-on experience with Finanzamt, BaFin, Bundesbank, ECB, KfW, Deutsche Rentenversicherung and the German mortgage market

cross_sample_system.dominant_pattern: Each video opens with a striking anecdote or historical event, converts it into a present-day parallel, exposes a hidden structural trap, escalates consequences from portfolio-level to life-level, then resolves with a practical protocol and a worldview shift.
what_is_repeated_across_samples: Title promises revelation plus correction of a false belief.
Cold open uses a vivid story, person or date cluster before the thesis.
Immediate pivot: 'this is happening again / right now / to you.'
Presenter positions himself as an obsessive researcher, not an entertainer.
Viewer is told mainstream advice is directionally true but dangerously incomplete.
Concepts are reduced to one central metaphor carried across the script.
Repeated contrast between spreadsheet math and human psychology.
Frequent use of named characters or mini-case studies to concretise abstractions.
Action steps appear after fear/diagnosis, never before.
Endings compress the message into 3 takeaways or a concise doctrine.
what_is_intentionally_avoided: No dry textbook exposition without emotional framing.
No jargon left untranslated for long.
No absolute certainty; uses probabilistic seriousness.
No purely technical CTA; CTAs are embedded as practical tools, not hard sells.
No celebratory finance-bro energy, no luxury signalling, no macho alpha posture.
No references to exclusively American institutions or products (401k, Roth IRA, Social Security, Fannie Mae) without translation to German equivalents.
exceptions_used_strategically: Video 4 is simpler and more direct; less nuanced than the others because it targets urgency and beginner conversion.
Video 6 leans more speculative/conspiratorial but protects credibility with repeated disclaimers about lack of proof.
Video 7 is more constructive and motivational, but still framed through pain, misperception and psychological failure.
Video 8 focuses exclusively on the German property market and the traps of financing, taxes and rental post-2022.

rotation_mandate.purpose: Force thematic diversity across videos. Prevent the model from collapsing into real-estate/financing on every generation. The blueprint's terminology and sample set are real-estate-heavy; without an explicit rotation rule, the model defaults to property math, Bausparvertrag mechanics, Kaufnebenkosten, Grunderwerbsteuer and household debt because they satisfy the content formula most easily.
rotation_mandate.principle: Every generated script must be assigned to ONE category. Categories rotate. Consecutive videos must never share the same category. Real-estate has a hard cap.

categories.restriction: This category may appear at most once in every six consecutive videos. If any of the last two videos were in this category, skip it entirely and pick another.

selection_rules: Track the last six videos produced by the channel and their assigned categories.
Before generating a new script, choose the category that has been used LEAST recently. On a tie, prefer the category with fewer appearances in the last twelve videos.
Never generate two consecutive videos in the same category.
The real_estate_financing category has an additional hard cap: at most one in every six videos.
If the channel has no history (first video), default to one of: money_psychology, concentration_indexing, or macro_currency.
If the user has explicitly requested a topic, honour it, but flag the rule violation in a single sentence inside the script's internal notes (not in the script body).
rotation_mandate.user_command_override: The user's explicit topic request always wins, but the generation model must warn in one sentence if the request breaks the rotation rule (e.g., 'this will be your third real-estate video in a row').
anti_patterns_to_avoid: Do not default to real estate as the 'most visually compelling' or 'most urgent' category.

Do not use property metaphors (house, mortgage, lease, roof, foundation, door, key, Bausparvertrag, Eigenheim, Grundbuch) as the central metaphor for non-property categories. Use different physical metaphors instead: gansos, banheira, bola de neve, banco de três pernas, ponte, engrenagens, jardim, jarro, portão, poço, fogo, semente, tear, escada, mapa, bússola, rio, represa, âncora, muro, castelo, navio, motor, roda, espelho, eco, sombra, fio, corrente, farol, túnel, escada, rede, peneira, esponja, prisma, polia, válvula, fechadura, balança, carrinho de mão, mochila, reservatório, relógio, ampulheta, tear, moinho, âncora, ponte levadiça.
Do not reference interest rates, home prices, Grunderwerbsteuer, Kaufnebenkosten or housing markets as primary evidence in non-property categories.

Do not use the viewer's own home as the emotional anchor in non-property categories. Anchor instead to their salary, their Depot balance, their Riester, their savings, their time, their family, their career, or their future Rente.

click_drivers: identity relevance ('your money', 'you want to invest')
compressed certainty ('this is what to do')
reversal of common belief ('passive income isn't passive')
title_mechanics.number_usage: Years, percentages, counts and EUR figures increase perceived seriousness and intellectual legitimacy.
title_mechanics.title_psychology: The viewer clicks because the title suggests they are unknowingly exposed to a system-level risk that others are missing — and that the German system has specific vulnerabilities nobody is discussing.

implied_enemy: simplified mainstream advice (including some social-media gurus and property salesmen)
political institutions (Finanzamt, Bundesministerium der Finanzen, Bundesbank, ECB)
culture of excessive saving and risk aversion
implied_ally: regulators when they work (BaFin, Bundesbank, Verbraucherzentrale)

macro_flow: 1. Pattern interrupt opening: bizarre anecdote, historical collapse or jarring scenario with German relevance (1923 hyperinflation, 1948 monetary reform, Wirtschaftswunder, reunification, euro crisis, energy crisis, 2022 inflation, regional bank collapses).
2. Snap-link to present relevance: 'the same pattern is happening now.'
3. Presenter framing: why he is qualified / why this isn't hype.
4. Promise stack: explicit list of what the viewer will understand by the end.
5. Tool CTA early: free calculator/report framed as corrective utility.
7. Conceptual explanation with simple language and arithmetic.
9. Psychological complication: why humans fail even when the math works.
10. Concrete examples/case studies with named people and specific numbers in EUR.
12. Identity-level conclusion: freedom comes from mindset/system, not mere returns.
13. Final compression into takeaways + soft internal CTA to another video/subscribe.

opening_pattern.method: Start with a highly specific anecdote before the thesis so the viewer is mentally hooked by narrative, not argument.
opening_pattern.why_it_works: The viewer unconsciously asks 'why are you telling me this?' and the script answers by connecting the anecdote to their money/life.
opening_variants: German historical scandal/collapse (1923 Hyperinflation, 1948 Währungsreform, Neue Markt, Wirecard, Greensill, real-estate crisis)
ordinary person scenario with hidden flaw
Statistisches Bundesamt or Bundesbank data used as a shock

pacing_model.rhythm: Dense but segmented. Short-to-medium sentences dominate, broken by longer explanatory runs after hooks land.
pacing_model.acceleration_pattern: Hook -> explanation -> new danger -> deeper mechanism -> practical release.
retention_devices: forward promises ('here's what we're doing today')
counterintuitive turns ('the math works, human psychology doesn't')
alternation between macro and personal examples
references to familiar German institutions (Bundesbank, Finanzamt, BaFin, ECB, Deutsche Rentenversicherung)

dominant_shapes: Analogy sentence followed by translation sentence.
sentence_design.feel: Controlled urgency. The prose sounds like spoken thinking, but it is tightly engineered.
sentence_design.cadence_trick: Uses short punch lines after data-heavy passages to reset attention.

word_choice.language_behavior: Abstract finance terms are almost always paired with tangible verbs or objects. The object bank should include a WIDE RANGE of physical metaphors, not predominantly property-related ones: geese, bathtub, snowball, three-legged stool, bridge, gears, garden, jar, gate, well, fire, seed, loom, staircase, map, compass, river, dam, anchor, wall, castle, ship, engine, wheel, mirror, echo, shadow, thread, chain, lighthouse, tunnel, ladder, net, sieve, sponge, prism, pulley, valve, lock, scale, wheelbarrow, backpack, reservoir, mill, amphora, basket, hourglass.
word_choice.credibility_words: specific dates, named firms, exact percentages, German historical names, concrete EUR amounts

contrast_structure: average return vs sequence of return

tone_layering.deeper_emotional_register: betrayal by institutions, relief through understanding, dignity through disciplined realism

core_psychology: Uses fear, but not random fear; fear is tied to mechanism, making it feel intelligent rather than sensational.
Creates relief by converting vague anxiety into understandable structure.
Makes viewer feel smarter than the passive majority if they keep watching.
Uses anti-hype disclaimers to increase trust before making strong claims.
Frames action as self-defence, not greed.
Leverages specific knowledge of the German system (Rente, Bausparvertrag, ETF, real estate, Finanzamt, Abgeltungsteuer) to create a sense of insider knowledge.

methods: references institutions by name (Bundesbank, Finanzamt, BaFin, ECB, Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Statistisches Bundesamt, Sachverständigenrat)
calls out bad incentives rather than cartoon villains
translates documents/regulations into plain German (ETF-Sparplan rules, Abgeltungsteuer, Vorabpauschale, Riester, Rürup, mortgages, AfA, Mietpreisbremse)
cites Statistisches Bundesamt data, Bundesbank reports, federal budgets, Stiftung Warentest
credibility_engineering.effect: The narrator sounds like a sober insider decoding reality for outsiders.

curiosity_loops: Why doesn't the obvious strategy work?
What happens when the system breaks?
retention_psychology.tension_creation: Tension is built by showing the viewer they are exposed to a risk they previously thought was safety.
retention_psychology.relief_timing: Relief arrives only after the system is fully diagnosed, which increases perceived value of the solution.

beliefs: Most financial pain comes from incentives and psychology, not lack of information alone.
Institutions optimise for system preservation, not your well-being.
Conventional advice is often half-true and dangerous when decontextualised.
Freedom is more about flexibility, margin and enoughness than maximising returns.
The disciplined ordinary person can outperform the emotional crowd.
The German system has specific vulnerabilities that most mainstream advice ignores.
Understanding the interplay between Finanzamt, Bundesbank, ECB and the mortgage market is essential for financial safety in Germany.
Bausparvertrag is not automatically a superior strategy; it is a tool with opportunity costs.
Depending exclusively on the gesetzliche Rente is a systemic risk for most Germans.
Abgeltungsteuer and Vorabpauschale hit savers harder than most model.
Riester and Rürup are not efficient by default; they are products with caps, fees and lock-ins.
Eigentum is not the same as Mietrendite; a self-occupied home is a consumption good, not an investment.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.status_framing: High status is attached to calm realism, delayed gratification and structural understanding, not flashy consumption.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.fear_framing: The real danger is not one crash or one bad pick; it is building your life on false assumptions — especially about property, pensions and what the government will do next.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.transformation_promise: Move from reactive participant to system-aware allocator who can't be easily trapped — someone who understands the German rules better than the average German.

content_formula.step_1: Choose a financial topic with mainstream familiarity and hidden complexity, WITHIN the category assigned by the rotation_mandate (ETF-Sparplan, Bausparvertrag, Riester, Rürup, mortgage, property, Abgeltungsteuer, gesetzliche Rente).
content_formula.step_2: Find a German historical analogy, strange anecdote or sharp mini-story that mirrors the modern issue.
content_formula.step_3: Frame the common understanding as incomplete or dangerously naive.
content_formula.step_4: Introduce one sticky metaphor that can carry the full explanation. Prefer non-property metaphors unless the assigned category is real_estate_financing.
content_formula.step_5: Translate the mechanism into plain arithmetic with concrete EUR numbers.
content_formula.step_6: Add a human-failure layer: why people still mess this up even when the math is knowable.
content_formula.step_7: Insert one or more case studies with names, ages, incomes, balances, outcomes.
content_formula.step_8: Escalate from portfolio consequence to lifestyle, identity or societal consequence.
content_formula.step_9: Offer a protocol/ruleset that feels practical, not magical.
content_formula.step_10: End with worldview compression and a concise memorable doctrine.

stylistic_rules_for_future_outputs: Never explain a concept without an image/object/metaphor.
Use numbers to anchor trust, not to overwhelm.
Alternate macro systems and individual stories.
Speak as if correcting a dangerous misunderstanding.
Let skepticism and humility coexist: strong thesis, selective uncertainty.
Avoid sounding like a trader; sound like a strategic realist.
Give the viewer dignity through understanding, not through hype.
Use German-specific references (Finanzamt, Bundesbank, BaFin, ECB, Deutsche Rentenversicherung, budget, ETF-Sparplan, Abgeltungsteuer, etc.).
Avoid American financial terms (401k, Roth IRA, Social Security, 30-year fixed, FICO score, etc.) without translation.
title_generation_rules: Centre danger, reversal or hidden mechanism.
Use direct second-order implications: not just 'recession' but 'worse than a recession.'
Make titles feel like practical protection against a trap.
Include German specificity whenever possible ('your ETF-Sparplan', 'your Rente', 'Finanzamt', 'Abgeltungsteuer').
hook_generation_rules: Open on a vivid story or date cluster before introducing the topic.
Reveal the present-day relevance within the first 5–8 lines.
Promise a deeper mechanism, not just surface explanation.

video_1.blueprint: Freedom fantasy versus mechanical reality. Strong on metaphor, optionality, lifestyle creep, psychology of enough. German context: gesetzliche Rente, ETF-Sparplan, property, cost of living.

video_2.blueprint: Historical concentration mania repeated today. Strong on structural analogy, anti-indexing revisionism, explicit portfolio protocol. German context: concentration in DAX, automotive, chemicals, property, over-concentration in deposits and Bausparvertrag.

video_3.blueprint: Macro regime change. Strong on date-stacking, institutional references, currency/industry framing, existential stakes. German context: EUR, ECB, Bundesbank, industry, energy, debt, immigration, productivity.

video_4.blueprint: Policy move translated into household consequences. Simpler, more beginner-targeted, more direct villain/system framing. German context: federal budget, tax changes, Abgeltungsteuer, Vorabpauschale, Riester, Rürup, Wohnungsbauprämie, Mietpreisbremse.

video_5.blueprint: Generational systemic failure. Strong on metaphor (three-legged stool), demographic scaling, sympathy mixed with indictment. German context: gesetzliche Rente, Pflegeversicherung, healthcare, housing, debt, boomers vs millennials.

video_6.blueprint: Conspiracy-adjacent mechanism explained with legal/financial precedent. Strong on debt-spiral metaphor and disclaimer-based credibility protection. German context: national debt, QE, inflation, ECB, Bundesbank, securitisation, Target2.

video_7.blueprint: Slow boring compounding made emotionally compelling. Strong on motivational psychology without becoming inspirational fluff. German context: ETF-Sparplan, dividends, regular investing, patience, Vorabpauschale.

video_8_reference.blueprint: The German property financing and investment trap post-2022. Strong on fiscal math, regulatory shifts, buyer reality, promise-versus-reality contrast. Context: Beleihungsauslauf, Zinsbindung, Sondertilgung, Kaufnebenkosten, Grunderwerbsteuer, Notar, Grundbuch, AfA, Mietrendite, Mietpreisbremse, Spekulationssteuer, Eigenkapital.
video_8_reference.rotation_note: This sample exists as a reference for the real_estate_financing category ONLY. It must not be used as a template for other categories, and it counts against the 1-in-6 cap.

generation_instructions_for_another_mode.objective: Produce long-form German finance scripts that feel like hidden-system exposés rather than generic educational content.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.step_zero: Before writing anything, read rotation_mandate, determine the last six video categories, and select the least recently used category that respects the selection_rules. State the chosen category internally before drafting.
must_include: one category from rotation_mandate that respects the selection_rules
one strong metaphor (preferably non-property unless the category is real_estate_financing)
one German historical or structural parallel
one explicit false belief being corrected
German institutional references (Finanzamt, Bundesbank, BaFin, ECB, Deutsche Rentenversicherung)
German financial products (ETF-Sparplan, Bausparvertrag, Riester, Rürup, gesetzliche Rente, mortgages, property, Abgeltungsteuer, Vorabpauschale)
must_avoid: references to exclusively American institutions without German equivalents
defaulting to real estate when the category is not real_estate_financing
using house/mortgage/Bausparvertrag as the central metaphor in non-property categories
consecutive videos in the same category
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.success_condition: The final script should make the viewer feel simultaneously alarmed, intellectually satisfied and more in control — with a deeper understanding of the German financial system, AND it should belong to a category that has not been used recently.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.output_length_requirement: The final FULL SCRIPT must be strictly between 7,000 and 9,000 characters.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.output_length_verification: Before sending the answer, verify the FULL SCRIPT character count. If it is below 7,000 or above 9,000 characters, rewrite it until it falls within range.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.hard_fail_condition: Any FULL SCRIPT under 7,000 characters or over 9,000 characters is invalid and must be rewritten before output. Any FULL SCRIPT that violates the rotation_mandate selection_rules is also invalid and must be rewritten.
